messages.subject: Checking parameters for distributions
parts:
Regarding splitting out the checks, I think what Bob has suggested is
good, will work, and is what we should do. I was thinking about this
yesterday / today and wondering how to avoid duplicate checking.

This part got by me:
In fact, we could make checking a template boolean param with a
default to check the ranges.

How does that work?

On Tue, Nov 8, 2011 at 3:57 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> On 11/8/11 2:22 PM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
>> I think most distributions have sort of well defined behavior for
>> extreme parameter values—normals turn into deltas or improper uniforms
>> as sigma goes to 0 or inf, t's turn into normals or deltas as nu goes
>> to inf or 0, gammas turn into deltas as shape goes to 0 or rate goes
>> to inf, etc. IEEE math won't necessarily make these things happen like
>> they should by default. There's a little bit of a performance hit for
>> enforcing correct behavior, but it's probably pretty minor in c++
>> compared with evaluating logs and exps.
>
> We should definitely think about this for the distributions.
>
> If the performance hit's too much, we can have two versions
> of all of the functions, one that checks its params and one
> that doesn't.  In fact, we could make checking a template
> boolean param with a default to check the ranges.
>
> Daniel?
>

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Checking parameters for distributions
parts:
Template parameters can be primitives and they can
get defualts, so you'd do something like:

template <typename T, bool check_range=true>
T sqrt(T x) {
if (check_range) { ... do the check ... }
return sqrt(x);
}

now if you call

double x;
double y = foo<double>(x);

you get type checking. Same if
you call foo<double,true>(x);

But if you call

double x;
double y = foo<double,false>(x);

you don't get the checks.

- Bob

Awesome. Thanks for clarifying. Time to start implementing it that way.

Should we break out the checks into their own functions?
Pros:
- Less duplicate checking code (we only need to write the function
once per distribution)

- A user can choose to check the parameters outside of the calculation
of log probability
- Error checking logic is separate from the calculation.

Cons:
- Another function to maintain / document.
- Is this how we want others to extend the distributions?

Thoughts?


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Checking parameters for distributions
parts:
There's a bunch of questions open:

I don't think making users first call a check_normal()
function then the normal_log() is a good idea -- it's
too easy to make mistakes or forget to check. As I wrote
to Daniel in an earlier message, helper check functions
for things like positiveness are useful.

Several different options make sense to me:

1. Always check and just return NaN for illegal inputs.
This is what expressions like 0/0 do (I believe 1/0 returns
positive infinity, but I'd have to check).

Where possible, we can extend behavior to +/- infinity
as functions like log and exp do.

On that note, we should also check variables that aren't
used if we want to have similar behavior to built-in and
std lib arithmetic.

2. Allow checking to be configured. Sensible options
would be to (a) turn checking off, (b) return NaN,
(c) throw an excpetion, or (d) print a warning.

If we configure checking, I see two options, (i) do it
function-by-function, or (ii) configure everything
statically (probably Stan-wide if that's the way we go).
inputs (following the divide-by-zero behavior). Option (i)
is more flexible, but also more work to use for clients.

Let's not worry too much about our programming time for
these simple, repetitive kinds of things -- I'm totally happy
to pitch in with the bricklaying.

- Bob
